module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Erdős Problem 730

*References:*
  - [erdosproblems.com/730](https://www.erdosproblems.com/730)
  - [A129515](https://oeis.org/A129515)
-/

@[expose] public section
namespace Erdos730

abbrev S :=
  {(n, m) : ℕ × ℕ | n < m ∧ n.centralBinom.primeFactors = m.centralBinom.primeFactors}


/--
Are there infinitely many pairs of integers $n < m$ such that $\binom{2n}{n}$
and $\binom{2m}{m}$ have the same set of prime divisors?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_730 : answer(sorry) ↔ S.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
For example, $(87,88)$ and $(607,608)$ are such pairs.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_730.variants.explicit_pairs :
    {(87, 88), (607, 608)} ⊆ S := by
  rintro _ (rfl | rfl) <;> refine ⟨by decide, ?_⟩
  all_goals
    simp only [Nat.centralBinom, Nat.choose_eq_descFactorial_div_factorial]
    decide +kernel

/--
There are examples where $(n, m) ∈ S$ with $m ≠ n + 1$.

(Found by AlphaProof, although it was implicit already in [A129515])
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_730.variants.delta_ne_one : ∃ (n m : ℕ), (n, m) ∈ S ∧ m ≠ n + 1 := by
  dsimp [S]
  use 10003
  use 10005
  norm_num [Finset.ext_iff, Nat.choose_eq_zero_iff, Nat.centralBinom]
  simp_rw [Nat.choose_eq_descFactorial_div_factorial]
  intro p hp
  constructor
  all_goals exact fun h' => or_self_iff.1 (hp.dvd_mul.1 (
    h'.trans (by refine' of_decide_eq_true (by constructor : _ = ↑_))))


end Erdos730

status_issues.source_status: The current Erdős Problems page marks the problem SOLVED and credits an affirmative solution to GPT Pro, prompted by Price. The linked manuscript, dated June 24, 2026, states in Theorem 1.1 that infinitely many consecutive central binomial coefficients have the same prime-divisor set.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/730 says: “This was solved by GPT Pro (prompted by Price),” and reports ≫ x^{1/2} suitable n ≤ x. The linked source is https://www.overleaf.com/read/gpttrsmhbhbk#a7cfdf, Equal Radicals of Consecutive Central Binomial Coefficients, Theorem 1.1.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to research solved and replace answer(sorry) with answer(True), citing the linked solution. Keep the mathematical right-hand side unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for infinitely many pairs with n ≠ m, whereas S retains only pairs with n < m.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Equality of the prime-divisor sets is symmetric. If T denotes the source's distinct-pair set, then T = S ∪ Prod.swap '' S. Swapping is a bijection, so T is infinite exactly when S is infinite. This equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the admitted main theorem.

sources_consulted: Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa and Straus, On the prime factors of (2n choose n), Mathematics of Computation 29 (1975), 83–92, especially p. 91: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-27.pdf
GPT Pro, Equal Radicals of Consecutive Central Binomial Coefficients, dated June 24, 2026, introduction and Theorem 1.1: https://www.overleaf.com/read/gpttrsmhbhbk#a7cfdf
review.notes: Checked S and all three theorems. Lean proofs confirm that primeFactors equality is precisely equality of prime-divisor sets here, and that allowing index 0 adds no pairs: centralBinom 0 = 1, while every positive-index central binomial coefficient is divisible by 2. Computations confirmed (87,88), (607,608), and the common prime-factor sets at 10003, 10004, and 10005. Both auxiliary theorems are free of sorry dependencies. Experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and large_examples.lean compile successfully; the reviewed file was not modified.
